identities.known_blocker: The copular shape requires a DEFINITE/INDEFINITE determiner, and 'our' is a possessive — not in either received class. The copula is also contracted into 'Dinah’s', which the word tokenizer keeps as one token, so no copula is seen at all. Recorded as a prediction of failure, made before running.

frames.why: The Mouse RECITES a tale. Fury and the tale's mouse are beings inside that recitation, not members of the party on the bank. A reader that admits them to the chapter's cast, or merges the tale's mouse with the Mouse telling it, has crossed a frame boundary. bindNarrationFrames exists for exactly this and this driver passes ONE frame for the whole chapter, so this is a predicted failure.

frames.quote: William the Conqueror, whose cause was favoured by the pope
frames.why: The Mouse reads aloud from a history book. William, Edwin, Morcar, Stigand and Edgar Atheling are named inside that recitation. They are real propositions of the recited text, not events of this chapter — a distinction the ledger currently has no way to draw.

predicted_failures: Dinah's our cat will not fire (possessive determiner + contracted copula), so chapter 1's open identity expectation will NOT be fulfilled even though the corroboration is right there.
Six intransitive propositions above (cheered, bowed, choked, moved off, and others) cannot be admitted while relations.js requires both a subject group and an object group (S90).
The old Crab and the young Crab share the surface 'Crab' and will likely fold into one referent.
The two embedded frames will be read as chapter events.
